headline: Cyclone Murasu: All 70 gates of Prakasam Barrage opened; 71,000 cusecs released into Krishna
content: VIJAYAWADA Heavy rain continues in the Krishna basin under the influence of Cyclone Murasu. The Water Resources Department (WRD) has suspended water supply to canals and opened all 70 gates of the Prakasam Barrage to send the surplus flow downstream. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/cyclone-murasu-landfall-live-updates-november-3-2026-rain-andhra-pradesh-telangana-odisha-weather/article71659195.ece The Prakasam Barrage was receiving 71,000 cusecs at 8 a.m. on Wednesday, and the entire quantity was being released into the Krishna river towards the Bay of Bengal. The water level stood at 12 feet. Floodwater flows through the open gates of the Prakasam Barrage across the Krishna in Vijayawada on Wednesday. All 70 gates have been opened after two days of heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu. Video: K.V.S. Giri https://t.co/GtrzTzb0N2— The Hindu - Andhra Pradesh (@THAndhra) November 4, 2026 To facilitate the discharge, 30 gates had been raised by two feet and another 40 by one foot. WRD officials have stopped releases into the Krishna Eastern, Krishna Western and Guntur canals as a precaution against possible flooding. Cyclone Murasu updates: Two dead, 52,459 hectares of crops damaged in A.P. Cyclone Murasu updates: Two dead, 52,459 hectares of crops damaged in A.P. Cyclone brings heavy rain to Prakasam and Palnadu districts; wind speed during landfall was 110-120 kmph, says IMD; 12,230 people are in rehabilitation centres in Guntur, Bapatla, and Palnadu districts; preliminary reports estimate losses of ₹344 crore The inflows are being fed largely by the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams, which drain into the Krishna from the local catchment areas. Surplus releases from the barrage began on Tuesday night after inflows increased. The decision to regulate the discharge comes amid reports of exceptionally heavy rainfall in NTR district and forecasts of more rain by the India Meteorological Department. Officials are keeping a close watch on the river’s inflows and the situation in the upstream catchment areas. Residents in low-lying settlements along the Krishna riverbanks have been asked to exercise caution and comply with instructions from the authorities. Cyclone Murasu: Ramanaidu puts irrigation officials on high alert over swollen rivers, drains Cyclone Murasu: Ramanaidu puts irrigation officials on high alert over swollen rivers, drains The Nallamada and Parchur drains are flowing above their maximum levels around Parchur, Bapatla and Chirala Cyclone Murasu: Ramanaidu puts irrigation officials on high alert over swollen rivers, drains storyline 1 Heavy rain across central districts Edlapadu in Palnadu district received the most rain in the State in the 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Wednesday, 269.45 mm, according to the Andhra Pradesh Directorate of Economics and Statistics (APDES). Sixteen automatic weather station gauges in the state stations crossed 204.5 mm mark, the India Meteorological Department (IMD)’s threshold for extremely heavy rain. In NTR district, Chintalapadu in Tiruvuru mandal recorded 178.25 mm. Ghantasala in Krishna district got 222.75 mm. Floodwater flows through the open gates of the Prakasam Barrage across the Krishna in Vijayawada on Wednesday. All 70 gates have been opened after two days of heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu. headline: Punjab govt announces 3% DA hike for 8 lakh employees, pensioners | Akashvani News
content: Punjab government has announced an increase of 3 per cent in the Dearness Allowance of its 8 lakh employees and pensioners today. Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann made this announcement during a press conference in Chandigarh. Terming it as a Diwali gift, he said the increased DA will be paid to the concerned with the December salary. He said that when his government came into power in 2022, the DA was 28 percent which has now gone up to 53 per cent. headline: Consider regulated timings for firecrackers, Bombay High Court tells Maharashtra government
content: Mumbai The Bombay High Court has asked the Maharashtra government to consider the applicability of the Supreme Court’s directions for regulated timings for bursting firecrackers during Deepavali to prevent severe environmental and health hazards in the city. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/maharashtra/ In a 13-page order, issued after taking suo motu note of the pulling down of a video of actress Dia Mirza on Deepavali by the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), a Bench of Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale referred to a set of directions issued by the Supreme Court on October 29, 2026 in the context of the high levels of pollution prevailing in the Delhi-NCR region during the festive season. Watch: Bombay High Court orders BMC to re-upload Dia Mirza firecracker appeal video video 1 Row over Dia Mirza’s appeal for a noise-free Deepavali | Explained Row over Dia Mirza’s appeal for a noise-free Deepavali | Explained The BMC uploaded the videos on November 1, but soon after the video of actor Dia Mirza went up, BJP Mumbai president Ameet Satam is learnt to have called the BMC administration to pull it down Row over Dia Mirza’s appeal for a noise-free Deepavali | Explained storyline 1 The High Court order, which was made available on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), said that the Court was of the opinion that it would also be appropriate for the State government and other authorities, including the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board, the BMC, and the Police Department, to consider these directions, particularly in regard to the timings for bursting firecrackers. The Supreme Court had directed that the bursting of approved green crackers during Deepavali be restricted to specific windows between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. in the National Capital Region (NCR). Supreme Court calls Deepavali fireworks a ‘religious practice’, allows green crackers for two days in Delhi-NCR storyline 1 BJP forces BMC to pull down Dia Mirza’s video on eco-friendly Deepavali BJP forces BMC to pull down Dia Mirza’s video on eco-friendly Deepavali Mayor says, administration should take clearance on the list of celebrities in the future; Mirza says, video was in public interest, as per Bombay High Court order; Opposition slams BJP for being religiously divisive BJP forces BMC to pull down Dia Mirza’s video on eco-friendly Deepavali storyline 1 “In our opinion, it would be appropriate for the State government and the authorities concerned in Maharashtra to consider the applicability and implementation of the said directions in the State, having regard to the prevailing local conditions,” the Court said. The apex court had recently underscored that while Deepavali is a joyous national festival celebrated across communities, the unregulated bursting of firecrackers poses severe environmental and health hazards. “It can trigger sharp spikes in the Air Quality Index (AQI) and generate microscopic particulate matter (PM) that remains trapped in the atmosphere for days,” the Supreme Court had said. Bombay HC slams BMC removal of Dia Mirza’s Deepavali video, says secularism governs festival participation Bombay HC slams BMC removal of Dia Mirza’s Deepavali video, says secularism governs festival participation Bombay High Court tells BMC to re-upload actor’s video; her participation in a BMC campaign for a firecracker-free Deepavali came under fire from BJP, Shiv Sena politicians on religious grounds Bombay HC slams BMC removal of Dia Mirza’s Deepavali video, says secularism governs festival participation storyline 1 In the same order, the High Court termed the deletion of actor Dia Mirza’s social media awareness message against firecrackers “most unfortunate”, and observed that there is no room for factionalism or individualism when public health and environmental initiatives are undertaken in pursuance of court orders. The Bench lauded Dia Mirza and other prominent public figures, including Madhuri Dixit, Nishigandha Wad, Ajinkya Rahane, Harshada Khanwilkar, Swapnil Joshi, and Kushal Badrike, for voluntarily stepping forward without remuneration to support the public health and environmental campaign. While the hearing took place on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), the BMC has still not uploaded the video of the actress. The High Court held that it would be “ideal and eminently desirable” for the municipal corporation to restore the deleted post on its official handles, emphasising that Mumbai’s rich cultural heritage survives on the spirit of togetherness. Taking serious note of the incident where Dia Mirza’s message was singled out and taken down from the municipal body’s social media page, the Bench remarked that such reactions appeared to have overlooked the “overarching intent, object, and solemnity” of the court’s orders aimed at curbing air and noise pollution. “There can be no scope or justification for such reactions of a few individuals, particularly when such reactions are ex facie against the highest constitutional principles of secularism, which are paramount and to be adhered to by every citizen,” the Bench held. Sounding a note of caution to public authorities and machinery of the State, the court emphasised that every official action must be guided solely by the objective of nurturing goodwill and respecting every member of the community, irrespective of caste, community, or religion. “It is essential to foster an environment of fraternity and mutual respect, while recognising that the celebration of any festival is a constitutional right of every citizen,” the court observed, citing Supreme Court precedents that no individual ought to be isolated from celebrations. While reiterating its appreciation for the municipal administration’s anti-pollution measures, the Court said restoring the deleted awareness videos would align with constitutional norms and close the chapter on a positive note. The High Court hearing had come after Dia Mirza’s video sparked a political row, leading the BMC to selectively remove her clip from social media, following Mumbai BJP chief Ameet Satam’s objection and mayor Ritu Tawde’s comments labelling her “anti-Hindu”. While her clip urging people to avoid noise and air pollution was pulled down, campaign videos featuring actors Madhuri Dixit and Nishigandha Wad, as well as cricketer Ajinkya Rahane, remained on the BMC’s X and Instagram handles.

headline: Two-Day BIS Awareness Training Programme for Executive Engineers of Assam P&RD Department concludes in Guwahati
content: The two-day Training Programme on BIS Awareness for Executive Engineers of the Panchayat and Rural Development (P&RD) Department, Government of Assam, concluded on 3rd November 2026 at the Golap Borbora State Institute of Panchayat and Rural Development (GBSIPRD), Kahikuchi, Guwahati. The programme was organised by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), Guwahati Branch Office, in collaboration with GBSIPRD, Government of Assam, on 2nd and 3rd November 2026. A total of 35 Executive Engineers from various districts of Assam participated in the programme, which aimed to enhance their awareness and understanding of Indian Standards, quality requirements of construction materials, standardised construction practices and the importance of BIS-certified products in rural infrastructure development. Eight technical sessions were conducted during the two-day programme, with experts from Assam Engineering College (AEC), Guwahati, delivering key lectures. The technical sessions focused on various aspects of quality assurance in construction, disaster-resilient construction through modern construction techniques, procurement of BIS-certified products and the integration of quality standards and material strength into construction and infrastructure development. The sessions were conducted by Dr. Rajdeep Paul and Ms. Ankita Roy Karmakar, Assistant Professors, Department of Civil Engineering, Assam Engineering College. The speakers shared their technical expertise and practical insights on the application of Indian Standards in construction activities. The valedictory session was attended by Shri Ananta Kumar Gogoi, ACS, Additional Secretary to the Government of Assam, Panchayat and Rural Development Department, and Director, GBSIPRD. Shri Anupam Dutta, Joint Director, GBSIPRD, Assam, served as the Course Coordinator and facilitated the organisation and coordination of the training programme on behalf of the Institute. The programme highlighted the significance of integrating Indian Standards and quality assurance mechanisms into government infrastructure projects, particularly in the rural development sector, to ensure safety, durability, reliability and overall quality of construction.

headline: Congress wants to 'normalise, recognise and formalise' outsiders: JP Nadda slams Opposition
content: Bhopal: Union minister J P Nadda on Wednesday hit out at the Congress for opposing the SIR, and claimed that it wants to 'normalise, recognise and formalise' outsiders as they helped the party remain in power for a long time. .Addressing the 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) rally and 'padyatra' (foot march) here, he also said that the BJP supports detection, deletion and deportation of outsiders, and accused the Congress of trying to undermine the institution of the Election Commission of India (ECI). ."BJP's Amit Shah favours 'detect, delete and deport'. And what does Congress say? What does INDIA bloc say? They say 'normalise, recognise and formalise'. These people who have come from outside, normalise them. Make Aadhaar cards for them, make ration cards for them, settle them down," he alleged. ."They are your voters, recognise them and formalise them, make them part of Indian politics. Tell me, should we detect them or not? Should we deport them or not?" he said, urging the people to "delete" the Congress and the INDIA bloc. ."The Congress is trying to undermine the Election Commission of India, an institution that serves a nation which is often called the mother of democracy, where democratic values run through the veins of its people, and which has earned global recognition through years of dedicated efforts," he said. .The opposition party was doing so without any noble intent. Rather, it stems from its failure to garner public support, Nadda added. .Oppn trying to vitiate atmosphere despite EC exposing their lies on SIR: J P Nadda."Realising that the electorate is unlikely to grant them any space in the political landscape for the next 20 to 30 years, they have resorted to blaming the Election Commission," he said. ."The narrative they are trying to construct is that if the Congress wins, as they did in Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh, then 'Rahul Baba' is a champion. But if they lose elections, then the Election Commission is termed as dishonest," the Union Health Minister said. .In many parts of the world, voters must go to an election office to register their names. In India, however, a Booth Level Officer (BLO) goes door-to-door to facilitate voter registration and this is the strength of the Election Commission, according to him. .Citing the remark made recently by Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, he said the opposition party leaders were attacking in a "derogatory manner" to hide their electoral failures. .Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav also attacked the Congress for raising the issue of SIR, saying it was doing so to hide its electoral failures. .The BJP leaders later took part in the padyatra along with a large number of BJP workers.

headline: Not 'princes' but 'sons of soil' Modi, Yogi will lead India: Nitin Nabin flays Oppn
content: Gorakhpur: Not "so-called princes" but "sons of the soil", Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath would lead the country, BJP national president Nitin Nabin asserted, as he slammed the Opposition in a "pro-democracy" pitch here on Wednesday to counter its "vote chori" campaign alleging electoral irregularities. .Addressing an NDA coalition's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' campaign in Gorakhpur amid the presence of alliance partners Nishad Party and RLD, Nabin accused opposition parties of making excuses for their electoral defeats and said today's youth have rejected such political heirs. .Nitin Nabin leads BJP's protest march in Kolkata against 'anarchy' by opposition parties.Nabin trained his guns particularly at Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, whom he dubbed as a "part-time politician" active only during elections, unlike BJP workers who continued public service throughout the year. .He also slammed Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, calling them also "yuvraj". ."Rahul Gandhi, Indian democracy is so powerful that however many 'tathakathit Yuvraj' (so-called princes) like you emerge, they will come and go. It is the sons of this soil, Modi and Adityanath, who will lead the country," he said, claiming that the two leaders enjoyed the confidence of 140 crore people and had worked for their welfare. .Referring to the I.N.D.I.A. bloc's November 1 rally in Delhi, he claimed that it failed to draw even 10 per cent of the crowd its organisers had projected. .In contrast, he said, the BJP and its NDA allies were holding large marches in districts and towns across the country, which, according to him, reflected the alliance's strength and public support. .Nabin said Gandhi could "continue to spread lies", but the country had changed under PM Modi. .He said 140 crore people regarded Modi as their PM and as a "chowkidar" protecting their homes, families and the country. .On the opposition's allegations concerning the SIR exercise, Nabin said parties that had lost elections were blaming the revision instead of examining their own organisational weaknesses. .He asked why they had suffered electoral defeats before 2025 as well, when the current SIR exercise had not been conducted. .Nabin also referred to the Election Commission's challenge to Gandhi to demonstrate alleged EVM manipulation at a venue of his choice, claiming that the Congress leader did not accept the challenge and left the field. .Referring to the Bihar elections, Nabin claimed that Gandhi had already left the political field after the publication of the electoral rolls. .He also targeted Tejashwi Yadav, referring to him as the "prince of Bihar", and said young voters were rejecting such leaders. .The BJP chief questioned the opposition's claim that around 13 crore names had been removed from electoral rolls. Citing figures during his address, he claimed that 2.5 crore entries related to deceased voters and around six crore to people who had shifted from their registered addresses. .He also claimed that over three crore people could not be contacted to verify their addresses. .He further alleged that around three crore "infiltrators" were in the voter list and accused opposition parties of trying to protect them for electoral gains. .Nabin also invoked Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's analogy of a student repeatedly making excuses for failing examinations to slam the opposition. .For Gandhi, whom Adityanath compared with a failed rocket launch, the BJP chief said "not only the rocket but even its launching pad was faulty, producing leaders who repeatedly failed to make an electoral impact". .He also accused opposition leaders of questioning the Election Commission and alleging EVM manipulation instead of accepting electoral verdicts. .Accusing the Congress of failing to fulfil its promise of eradicating poverty, Nabin alleged that the party had instead kept poor people away from development. He contrasted its record with the work undertaken under Modi and Adityanath, claiming that both the country and UP were progressing under their leadership. .He accused the opposition of failing to learn from electoral defeats and resorting to what he described as crocodile tears and excuses. .Nabin accused the Congress and its allies of disrespecting the Constitution, alleging that the party had changed laws to nullify the Allahabad High Court's verdict against Indira Gandhi's election. .He also claimed the Nehru-Gandhi family had humiliated BR Ambedkar by working against his electoral victories, despite now invoking the Constitution to lecture others. ."Today, they go around carrying copies of the Constitution and lecture others on it," he said. .Nabin accused Gandhi and Yadav of staying indoors during COVID-19 while BJP workers helped people. He also claimed they initially opposed the "Modi vaccine" but later took it, expressing confidence in voters rejecting the opposition. .Warning against attempts to destabilise the country, Nabin said, "India's democracy is strong, its roots are deep, and your nefarious intentions will never succeed." .He also questioned the opposition's selective criticism of democracy, asking why it celebrated electoral victories in Himachal Pradesh and Karnataka but questioned democratic institutions after defeats in Haryana, Maharashtra and Bihar. .Targeting Gandhi's leadership, Nabin claimed Congress leaders were unhappy with his decisions but unable to challenge the Nehru-Gandhi family. .'Acting at behest of foreign powers': BJP chief Nitin Nabin slams Rahul Gandhi over Ramlila Maidan rally.He remarked, "If Rahul Gandhi continues to lead in this manner, I would say congratulations to the Congress. A time will come when there will be nobody left even to take the party's name." .Accusing the opposition of challenging the people's mandate, Nabin alleged that Gandhi was being used as part of a "foreign toolkit" to destabilise the country. He said more than 100 BJP-NDA marches had been organised across Uttar Pradesh to demonstrate public support for the alliance. .Nabin also questioned the opposition's "moral authority" to criticise PM Modi, citing development work in Amethi and Kerala. He said Modi had served with dedication and commitment for 25 years, questioning the opposition's "record" in challenging his leadership.

headline: Nauni University Establishes Cannabis Research Centre, Giving Boost to Himachal's 'Green to Gold' Initiative
content: Solan: Himachal Pradesh is taking steps towards developing cannabis as a regulated medicinal and industrial resource, with Dr YS Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry (UHF), Nauni, establishing a dedicated Centre on Cannabis Research with financial support from the state government. The centre has been established to advance scientific research, quality assessment, conservation and sustainable utilisation of cannabis for medicinal purposes. It will provide an institutional platform for research and development in a field that has gained increasing attention as the state explores the economic potential of regulated cannabis cultivation. The initiative is significant in view of the Himachal Pradesh government’s broader efforts to move beyond the traditional perception of cannabis as an illicit crop and explore its medicinal and industrial applications through scientific research and regulatory safeguards. The university’s research initiative also comes at a time when the state government is moving forward with its ‘Green to Gold’ initiative, aimed at promoting regulated industrial hemp cultivation and creating new economic opportunities for farmers. The state government’s approach towards cannabis cultivation has witnessed several important developments. In January 2025, the state Cabinet approved a pilot project to explore the potential of controlled cannabis cultivation for medicinal, scientific and industrial purposes. Dr YS Parmar University, Nauni, and Chaudhary Sarwan Kumar Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya, Palampur, were entrusted with research-related responsibilities. Subsequently, in June 2026, the state Cabinet approved amendments to the Himachal Pradesh Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Rules, 1989, paving the way for regulated cultivation, processing, manufacturing, storage and transportation of cannabis for medicinal and scientific purposes.

headline: Five Hacks Every Una Watch User Should Know
content: The Una watch is pretty much made to be hackable, with its interchangeable parts and open development environment. But it’s also pretty barebones at launch, without many features available yet. However, here are five things I’ve discovered I can do with it—and I hope to expand this list quite a bit as the device and its community mature. UNA Watch $199.00 at UNA Get Deal Get Deal $199.00 at UNA Charge the Una watch from your phoneBecause the Una watch has a regular USB-C port, you don’t need to remember any specific cable, dongle, or adapter to charge it. I knew that, but it didn’t occur to me until recently that I didn’t need a computer or a wall outlet to plug into the other end. I was able to take a USB-C to USB-C cable—the same kind I might carry around to charge my phone—and plug one end into my watch and the other into my phone. It charged! (You can also charge some other devices from a phone, including an Apple Watch, but you’d need to carry around that specific adapter, which is why nobody bothers.)Use HabitLab to get a recovery scoreThe Una watch doesn’t have any built-in sleep tracking, but a few community-built apps aim to provide it. The Slumber app, for example, will let you know how long you slept and compare your most recent bedtime with when you usually get to bed. There are no sleep stages (honestly: refreshing, since watches are rarely good at this anyway), and the analysis is done on the watch itself. But if what you’re really hoping for is a recovery score or an overnight HRV reading, the HabitLab app combines that with habit tracking. Every evening, the watch will buzz and ask you to check off which habits or factors played into your day: Alcohol and late meals are among the options, and the watch will automatically detect morning or evening workouts to add them to the list. In the morning, the watch asks you how you slept, and then it gives you a score based on your resting heart rate, HRV, and your subjective rating. The app is supposed to be able to put together trends and insights from this data, but I haven’t managed to get it to do this. Maybe it’s waiting for more data (I’ve been using it a little over a week), or maybe it’s just buggy. Put your library card on your Una watchBy contrast, the barcode app worked even better than I expected it to. It’s meant for a parkrun barcode; each participant in the free weekly 5K has a number that you can use to check your results online. But it works just as well for other barcodes. I installed the Barcode app and entered the number for my library card. Perhaps because of the watch’s MIP screen, I found this barcode scanned more reliably than any barcodes I’ve previously tried to use on a watch. The library scanner picked it up just fine on the first try, and a phone-based scanner also had no problem with it. You can store up to six barcodes, so I’ve also entered a few others, like my grocery discount card. The app supports QR codes as well as regular barcodes, and to enter a QR code, you just type in a shortened URL. (It needs to be 22 characters or less.) This means that the Barcode app is also a QR code creator, a nifty feature indeed.See how little daylight you have leftSeeing how soon the sun sets is a bit of a downer as we leave daylight saving time and get into the dark winter months, but it’s also helpful in planning. The Sun & Moon Face puts a graphic on your wrist that shows how far along the sun is in its trajectory across the sky for the day. When evening is approaching, you’ll see just how little time you have left. The app grabs your GPS location once a day, which means that for the first few hours I wore it, the sunrise and sunset times were incorrectly listed as 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. But as long as you aren’t flying to a drastically new location every day, the app does the job just fine. As a bonus, it changes the color of the screen’s sky to show daylight, nighttime, or sunrise/sunset colors. Download the developer toolkit and build somethingIf you want to hack this hackable watch, you might as well take the plunge and try to build something yourself. Instructions are here to download the development tools for Windows, Mac, or Linux, and there are tutorials for different features you might want to use and implement. There are also about a dozen example apps you can build on, including activity trackers, watch faces, and glances. I'm not much of a coder myself, but this is the friendliest setup I've seen for someone to get into building their own apps for a watch.

headline: In Chamba, CM announces civil court for Chowari, cash assistance for poor women
content: Shimla: Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Tuesday announced the opening of a civil court at Chowari in the Bhatiyat assembly constituency of Chamba district.He also announced the opening of CBSE-affiliated schools in the area based on local demands. In addition, Sukhu announced financial assistance of Rs 10 crore for various road projects in the constituency.The CM made these announcements while addressing a public meeting at Chowari Chowgan in the Bhatiyat assembly constituency.He said the state govt would launch the ‘Mukhyamantri Ka Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojana’ from next month to provide financial assistance of Rs 1,500 per month to eligible women from poor families.Under the scheme, the CM said beneficiaries would also receive 300 units of free electricity per month and free medical treatment through health insurance cards.He added that around 20,000 women from 10,000 eligible families in the Bhatiyat constituency would benefit from the scheme.Sukhu said it was the first time in Himachal Pradesh’s history that a govt had adopted a vision specifically focused on strengthening the rural economy. The state govt is providing a minimum support price of Rs 150 per kg for raw turmeric, Rs 80 per kg for wheat and Rs 50 per kg for maize. The state govt is also providing a support price of Rs 61 per litre for cow milk and Rs 71 per litre for buffalo milk, nearly double the earlier rates, he said.The CM further said the state govt had also undertaken significant reforms in the health sector to ensure access to state-of-the-art medical facilities up to the rural areas. He said that Rs 190 crore had been allocated for the smooth functioning of Chamba Medical College, besides providing 32 postgraduate seats in the college.The previous BJP govt opened several health and educational institutions without ensuring the availability of the required staff. In contrast, the present govt rationalised educational institutions and filled thousands of vacant teaching posts, he said.To provide quality education to students in rural areas, the state govt opened at least two or three CBSE-affiliated schools in every Vidhan Sabha segment and recruited over 2,700 teachers strictly on merit, Sukhu said.He also claimed that more than 100 schools were being upgraded to the CBSE pattern, for which teaching staff posts had already been advertised. The CM said that due to his govt’s pragmatic efforts, the state ranked fifth in providing quality education to students in 2025, compared to 21st in 2021 during the tenure of the BJP govt.A two-minute silence was also observed during the public meeting to pay respects to MLA and chairperson of the 7th State Finance Commission Nand Lal, who passed away on Tuesday, and Youth Congress functionary Chandermani Kulethi, who died in a tragic incident recently.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Police seize drug trafficker’s property worth Rs 48.3 lakh in Himachal’s Kangra
content: Shimla, Nov 4 (PTI) Himachal Pradesh Police has seized an alleged drug trafficker’s property worth Rs 48.30 lakh in Kangra district, officials said on Wednesday. This is the first physical possession of a forfeited property under the PIT NDPS Act in favour of the government, the police officials said. The action was taken against Shamsher Singh, a resident of Damtal in Indora tehsil of Kangra. According to police, the competent authority and administrator, SAFEM (FOP) Act, 1976, and NDPS Act, 1985, New Delhi, had ordered the forfeiture of the assets of the accused under sections 68-I(1) and 68-I(3) of the NDPS Act, free from all encumbrances. “The confiscated assets include a two-storey residential building located in Chhanni village of Indora tehsil, comprising the ground floor, first floor and basement, valued at Rs 45,90,557. Besides, cash amounting to Rs 2,40,440, allegedly generated through the illegal drug trade, was also forfeited,” police said. The attachment order was issued by the competent authority under Section 68-U of the NDPS Act on October 22 and the Damtal police station had formally served the order on the accused. The station house officer was authorised to take physical possession of the forfeited property.

headline: APEDA Facilitates Export of 1.3 MT of Sinduri Pomegranates from Kullu to Dubai
content: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, facilitated the export of 1.3 metric tonnes (MT) of Sinduri variety pomegranates from Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh to Dubai, United Arab Emirates (UAE). The consignment, comprising 650 boxes of 2 kg each, was exported by Uttar Pradesh-based Amama Exports. The initiative connects local growers and a Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) with an exporter, creating opportunities for Himachal Pradesh’s horticultural produce to access international markets. headline: Jai Ram Thakur leads BJP’s ‘Save Democracy’ march in Mandi, hits out at Sukhu govt over debt, disaster response
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) organised a massive protest march under the banner of ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ here today, with a large number of party workers and supporters from Mandi and Kullu districts participating in the demonstration. The march began at Paddal Ground and proceeded through the town before culminating at Seri Stage.Former chief minister and Leader of Opposition Jai Ram Thakur led the protest and launched a sharp attack on the state government, accusing it of misgovernance, unfulfilled election guarantees and insensitivity towards disaster-affected families.Addressing the gathering at Seri Stage, Thakur also criticised the Congress party’s allegations of vote theft and its opposition to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He defended the Election Commission and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, arguing that electoral processes must be respected by all political parties. He challenged Congress leaders and opposition MPs questioning electoral outcomes to resign from their positions if they genuinely lacked faith in the electoral system.Targeting Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Thakur questioned the government’s decision to organise celebrations to mark three years in office at Paddal Ground despite the devastation caused by natural disasters across Himachal Pradesh. He claimed that more than 450 people had lost their lives in disaster-related incidents and alleged that over Rs 10 crore was spent on the celebrations instead of showing sensitivity towards affected families.He also criticised the Chief Minister for attending a celebratory programme in Chamba despite the death of a Congress legislator from the Rampur Assembly constituency, calling it an example of political insensitivity.On the political situation in the state, Thakur claimed that BJP had performed strongly in recent local body elections. He said BJP candidates had secured the chairperson and vice-chairperson positions in 11 of the state’s 12 district councils, while the party had also secured victories in three of the four municipal corporations where elections were contested on party symbols.Thakur accused the Congress government of failing to fulfil its election guarantees, particularly the promise of Rs 1,500 monthly assistance to eligible women and employment opportunities for youth. He questioned the government’s criteria for selecting beneficiaries and demanded clarity on the promises made to the people.Raising concerns over the state’s financial position, he claimed that Himachal Pradesh’s outstanding debt had crossed Rs 1.20 lakh crore, compared with approximately Rs 69,000 crore when he was Chief Minister.Thakur also targeted Congress leader Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over the SIR issue and their comments against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Chief Election Commissioner of India.Former ministers Govind Singh Thakur and Suresh Bhardwaj, MLAs Rakesh Jamwal, Inder Singh Gandhi, Puran Chand Thakur, Dilip Thakur and Prakash Rana, along with other BJP leaders and party workers, participated in the protest. Mandi Sadar BJP MLA Anil Sharma was absent from the rally.Thakur expressed confidence that BJP would return to power in the 2027 Assembly election, asserting that the party would aim to win all 10 Assembly seats in Mandi district.

headline: November Heat Breaks Records in Himachal; Una Sizzles at 34.2°C
content: Shimla – Himachal Pradesh is witnessing an unusual spell of warm weather in November, with temperatures remaining significantly above normal across most parts of the state. The impact of changing weather patterns, coupled with the influence of the El Niño phenomenon, has kept daytime temperatures unusually high, particularly in the lowland areas. Una district recorded a maximum temperature of 34.2°C on Tuesday, the highest November temperature recorded there in recent years, surpassing previous records. The maximum temperature in Una had reached 33.4°C in November 2024, while 33.1°C was recorded in November 2000. However, the mercury crossed both these marks on Tuesday, highlighting the persistence of unusually hot conditions even as winter approaches. The impact of the warm weather is also visible in other parts of the state. Maximum temperatures in Shimla, Kangra and Sundernagar have approached previous records, while daytime temperatures across most regions are being recorded around 2°C above normal. According to the temperature data, Una was the hottest place among the listed locations, recording 34.2°C, followed by Mandi at 28.6°C, Bilaspur at 28.5°C and Kangra at 28.4°C. Dharamshala recorded 26°C, Nahan 25.7°C and Solan 25.4°C. The maximum temperature in Shimla stood at 22°C, while Manali recorded 19.6°C. Interestingly, while bright sunshine is keeping daytime temperatures high, nighttime conditions in the higher reaches of the state remain considerably colder. Several high-altitude areas are already experiencing freezing temperatures. On Monday night, Kukumseri recorded a minimum temperature of -2.1°C, while the mercury in Keylong dropped to -1.1°C. Meanwhile, the Meteorological Department has forecast predominantly clear weather across Himachal Pradesh, with bright sunshine expected to continue until November 9. The weakening of a Western Disturbance is likely to keep weather conditions stable during this period.

headline: India plans world's highest railway station at 5,256 metres, above China's record; check route, cost and key challenges of Rs 1.31 lakh crore project
content: India's proposed railway link to Ladakh could set a new global record, with plans for a railway station at an altitude of around 5,256 metres above sea level. If completed along the proposed alignment, the station beneath the Tanglang La pass would overtake China's Tanggula railway station to become the world's highest railway station. The proposed Bilaspur-Manali-Leh railway line is a strategically important infrastructure project aimed at connecting Himachal Pradesh with Ladakh through the challenging Himalayan terrain. With an estimated cost of Rs 1.31 lakh crore and nearly 270 km of tunnels, the ambitious corridor would be among India's most challenging railway engineering projects. The proposed 489-km broad-gauge railway corridor will connect Bilaspur in Himachal Pradesh with Leh in Ladakh. The alignment is planned to pass through several important towns and locations, including Sundernagar, Mandi, Manali, Sissu, Darcha, Keylong, Sarchu, Pang, Rumtse, Upshi and Kharu before reaching Leh. Identified as a strategic project by the Ministry of Defence, the railway line is expected to improve connectivity to the strategically important Ladakh region. According to the railway ministry, the survey has been completed and the Detailed Project Report (DPR) prepared. The estimated project cost stands at approximately Rs 1.31 lakh crore. One of the biggest highlights of the proposed Bilaspur-Leh railway line is a station planned beneath the Tanglang La pass at an elevation of approximately 5,256 metres above sea level. If constructed at the proposed elevation, the station would surpass China's Tanggula railway station, located on the Qinghai-Tibet Railway at around 5,068 metres. This would give India the distinction of having the world's highest railway station. Tanglang La is already a prominent high-altitude mountain pass on the Manali-Leh highway. However, bringing railway infrastructure to this elevation would require complex engineering, particularly because of the region's harsh climate, difficult geology and challenging terrain. The proposed railway corridor is expected to include approximately 270 km of tunnels across its 489-km alignment. This means that more than half of the railway line could pass through underground sections, making tunnelling one of the most significant components of the project. Construction teams would have to deal with difficult geological formations, steep gradients, extreme temperatures and high-altitude conditions. The Himalayan region also presents considerable uncertainties related to rock stability, excavation and construction logistics. These factors could make the project particularly demanding in terms of both cost and execution. Currently, road and air transport are the primary means of reaching Leh from other parts of the country. The Manali-Leh highway is an important route, but its high-altitude stretches and weather conditions can disrupt movement, particularly during the winter months. A railway connection could provide an additional transportation option for passengers and goods while strengthening logistical connectivity to Ladakh. Its strategic importance is particularly significant given the region's location and defence requirements. The railway corridor could help improve the movement of essential supplies and equipment, subject to the infrastructure and operational arrangements eventually developed for the project. The challenges involved in expanding railway connectivity in Himachal Pradesh are also visible in the ongoing Bhanupali-Bilaspur-Beri railway project. The 63-km line is expected to improve connectivity in the state and forms part of the broader railway infrastructure development in the region. However, the project has encountered hurdles involving land acquisition and the state's financial contribution. In October 2026, the Himachal Pradesh High Court quashed the preliminary land acquisition notification, observing that the government had not complied with the statutory requirements for extending the deadline to issue the land acquisition declaration.

headline: Ziro farmers dispatch over 3,000 chrysanthemum bunches to New Delhi
content: Itanagar, Nov 5: Farmers in Ziro have taken a significant step towards expanding commercial floriculture in Arunachal Pradesh, with more than 3,000 bunches of locally grown chrysanthemums dispatched to New Delhi.The consignment was flagged off from the Mini Secretariat in Ziro by Ziro-Hapoli MLA Hage Appa in the presence of Horticulture Secretary Koj Riniya, Lower Subansiri Zilla Parishad Chairperson Hibu Dumi, Director of Horticulture Tobom Bam, Deputy Commissioner Oli Perme, departmental officials and local flower growers.More than 800 bunches of chrysanthemums had already been sold in the local market, indicating growing commercial opportunities for flower growers in the district.The flowers were cultivated by farmers under the technical guidance of District Horticulture Officer Hibu Dante, with support from the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH), a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.Addressing the gathering, Koj Riniya highlighted the department's efforts to provide market-oriented training in scientific package of practices and good agricultural practices to improve flower quality and meet market standards.She said the state government was focusing on expanding floriculture by leveraging Arunachal Pradesh's diverse agro-climatic conditions and market potential.The department has also partnered with the CSIR-Institute of Himalayan Bioresource Technology, Palampur, Himachal Pradesh, to provide technical training and build the capacity of farmers.Riniya informed that farmers in Ziro were also cultivating gypsophila, which is expected to be harvested in the coming weeks. She identified Azadpur Mandi in New Delhi as an important market avenue for strengthening market linkages and improving farmers' income.She further stated that a special provision for floriculture development had been incorporated into the state government's Budget announcement for 2026-27.MLA Hage Appa congratulated the farmers and the Horticulture Department on the successful dispatch. He encouraged growers to adopt scientific and market-oriented cultivation practices to enhance their income.The initiative is expected to improve market access for local flower growers and promote floriculture as a viable livelihood opportunity in Arunachal Pradesh.

headline: Kullu-born Lt. Gen Sushil Chander takes charge as Director General of Army’s Integrated Training
source: Achievements of Atal Medical and Research University
content: Lieutenant General Sushil Chander, a native of Katrain village in Himachal Pradesh’s Kullu district has made people of the state proud by becoming Director General of Integrated Training (DGIT) in the Indian Army. He assumed the charge at Headquarters of the Ministry of Defence (Army), New Delhi, on November 1. His elevation is a matter of pride for Himachal Pradesh, particularly Kullu district and his native village Katrain. He is also the first Lieutenant General from Sainik School Sujanpur Tihra to attain the rank. With over three-and-a-half decades of distinguished military service, Lt Gen Chander brings extensive experience in military logistics, strategic planning, administration and operational preparedness to his new assignment. An alumnus of Government High School, Katrain, and Sainik School Sujanpur Tihra, he joined the National Defence Academy in January 1988 and was commissioned from the Indian Military Academy in December 1991. He is also an alumnus of the Defence Services Staff College, Wellington, and the National Defence College, New Delhi. During his military career, he held several important command and staff appointments, including Commanding Officer of 11 Field Ordnance Depot, Brigadier Ordnance of a Strike Corps and Major General of Ordnance Services of a strategically important Army Command responsible for the northern frontier with China.
